bullets.title: September CPI due today: consensus 0.55% headline, 0.18% core MoM — market split on reaction
bullets.body: JPM forecasts headline CPI +0.55% m/m (3.6% YoY) and core +0.18% m/m (2.4% YoY), a deceleration from August's 0.3% core. 44% of investors expect risk-on reaction; 35% mixed/negligible; 21% risk-off. A lower core print would support rate-sensitive baskets, while an inline print may be overshadowed by Anthropic's analyst day.

bullets.title: Fed base case: 2 more hikes (Dec '26, Mar '27); peak funds rate ~4.65%
bullets.body: Fed base case has shifted to 85% odds of one more hike in 2026 with peak funds rate at ~4.65% vs ~4.85% in late September. Boston Fed's Collins says rate hikes likely needed before year-end; NY Fed's Williams says no hike needed in 2027 at this time. Financial conditions have tightened since end of August, led by mortgage rates and dollar strength.

bullets.title: Jefferies flags risk markets are mistaking energy/tariff price shock for persistent inflation
bullets.body: Jefferies argues current inflation is supply-driven (energy, tariffs), not demand-driven: September payrolls +29k, hourly earnings +3.0% YoY below headline CPI of 3.4% YoY, savings rate fell to 4.1%, consumer sentiment 46.3. The 10Y term premium rose from 45bps to 108bps over the past year, tightening conditions independently of the Fed. Central risk is weakening demand, not accelerating inflation.

bullets.title: Bank earnings signal resilient consumer: card spending +10-13% YoY, delinquencies falling
bullets.body: JPM, Citi, and WFC all report card spending up 10-13% YoY with delinquencies and charge-offs falling YoY. GS delivered the strongest Q3 beat ($17.01 EPS vs $13.07 cons) with equities revenue +72% YoY; JPM missed at $5.57 vs $5.92. All four banks describe the same macro: strong growth, resilient labor, sticky inflation, and energy-driven price pressure with a corporate maturity wall looming.

bullets.title: Goldman flags AI-related demand adding ~45bp to core PCE inflation, peaking ~50bp by YE2026
bullets.body: GS estimates AI capex is currently adding ~45bp to core PCE inflation, expected to peak ~50bp by YE2026 then fall to ~10bp by YE2027 as the investment cycle matures. AI/tech capex was described by bank CEOs as an 'extraordinary tech super cycle' and significant macro force.

bullets.title: SOX down 5-7 consecutive sessions — worst streak since mid-2025; AI sentiment deteriorating
bullets.body: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index has declined for 5-7 consecutive sessions (sources vary), the longest losing streak since May 2025, led by memory (MU, SNDK each down ~7%) and semicap names. Bearish sentiment driven by power scarcity concerns, frontier lab funding viability, and custom silicon from Meta/Google/Microsoft (Maia 300) raising risk of value shift away from Nvidia/AMD. Tech described as 'best for sale on desk last 5 days.'

bullets.title: ASML Q3 beat-and-raise: GM 57.5% (+350bps q/q), FY26 rev guided to €44-45B; capacity now insufficient for demand
bullets.body: ASML reported Q3 gross margin of 57.5% (vs 56% consensus), the biggest beat in 2+ years, and raised FY26 revenue guidance to €44-45B while guiding FY26 gross margin to 56% (up 93bps vs consensus). Critically, management signaled current 30% capacity growth targets for 2027-28 are insufficient to meet customer demand, with orders already booked into 2029-30. Stock reaction muted/negative as market disappointed by lack of FY27 EUV unit clarity (~85 systems guided vs ~90 buy-side expectation).

bullets.title: Semiconductor capex dollars rotating from OpEx beneficiaries (memory, semicap) to Mag7 hyperscalers
bullets.body: Jefferies explicitly flags semiconductor dollars rotating from memory, semicap, and networking into Mag7 cloud hyperscalers, noting they have been net buyers of Mag7 in 8 of the last 12 weeks. SK Hynix delays some HBM4 back-end equipment orders to 2027, while DDR4 is outpacing DDR5 capacity allocation amid HBM shifts.

bullets.title: Citi CIO survey: IT budgets +3.4% NTM; AI now 7% of enterprise IT spend; MSFT and AMZN primary beneficiaries
bullets.body: Global NTM IT budget growth expectations ticked up to +3.4% (from +3.3% in June), with US accelerating to +3.9% while EMEA moderated to +1.8%. AI now represents ~7% of enterprise IT budgets with 72% sourced from new budgets. Microsoft cited most frequently as vendor expected to gain AI spending share, followed by Amazon; 63% of CIOs anticipate AI-related headcount reductions.

bullets.title: MSFT Azure group pursuing 20% cost cuts across ~11,500-person division amid AI spending pressure
bullets.body: Reports indicate MSFT Azure group head is asking leaders to develop plans reducing costs by at least 20% across the division. Separately, Citi raises MSFT PT to $636, projecting ~2pt Azure beat in FQ1 accelerating to 46-47% YoY cc, with Azure AI contributing ~25pts of growth and FY27 capex expected at $237B (63% YoY vs Street $220B).

bullets.title: Digital ad environment better than expected: META raised to $860-$895 across desks on AI monetization
bullets.body: Multiple banks raised META price targets (GS to $860, UBS to $884, Citi to $895) citing AI-driven improvements in creative, targeting, and measurement. Ad checks point to better-than-expected 3Q digital ad environment with budget growth accelerating across Search, Social, and Video; YouTube described as standout. GOOGL ad trends healthy but stays Neutral at multiple desks given rising AI capex and GenAI search competition concerns.

bullets.title: GOOGL Gemini 4 Argon launches globally; ranks #1 on Vals Index across finance, coding, legal, tax
bullets.body: GOOGL released Gemini 4 Argon globally via API and the Gemini app at $2/million input tokens and $10/million output tokens. GOOGL ranks #1 on the Vals Index for model performance across finance, coding, legal, and tax. Stock up ~1.3% premarket.

bullets.title: Strong consumer data complicates CPI reaction: credit card spending matches Q2 hot levels
bullets.body: JPM, WFC, and Citi credit card spending growth running at 10.7%, 9.2%, and 10.7% YoY respectively — matching Q2 levels. Consumer slowing needed to respect economic speed limit but not yet occurring; Core Services ex-housing inflation above 3% level. Credit card delinquencies trending lower and retail sales remain firm.

bullets.title: Energy: WTI at $95.31 as Iran targets Persian Gulf shipping; IEA sees diesel shortages into 2027
bullets.body: WTI up 0.5% to $95.31 as Iran plans continued targeting of ships in the Persian Gulf; Houthis attacked Saudi Aramco HQ with limited fire damage. ROTH raises 2026 WTI forecast 8% to $85.50/bbl. IEA sees diesel shortages lasting into 2027 from Iran war supply disruption; jet fuel at $1,520/metric tonne (+90% vs March).

bullets.title: Power scarcity emerging as key 2028 constraint on US data-center expansion
bullets.body: Jefferies flags ~65 IT GW under construction (140% of installed capacity) and ~361 GW announced (~760%), with only 12.9 GW of new capacity expected in 2026 and 18 GW in 2027. Power availability cited by GS as emerging key constraint on US data-center expansion by 2028. AEP is investing $4B in a 702MW Bloom Energy fuel cell project for Google under a 20-year PPA, operational by end of 2028.

bullets.title: Hedge fund positioning: quality bias, large-cap over small-cap, discretionary shorts expanding
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley prime brokerage data shows hedge funds running lighter gross exposure with a quality bias and favoring large-cap over small-cap. Discretionary positioning declined; high-end consumer shorts expanded to the 41st percentile; brick-and-mortar longs at historical lows. JPM Retail basket down 8.7% from August peak with positioning at 37th percentile suggesting room for reversal.

bullets.title: 3Q26 earnings off to a solid start: S&P 500 EPS tracking +26.3% YoY, 77% beat rate
bullets.body: UBS reports 77% of S&P 500 companies reporting to date beat estimates, with 3Q EPS growth tracking +26.3% YoY. TECH+ group EPS growth running at 46.6% YoY led by NVDA at +89%. Energy sector expected to grow 124.7% YoY. Key upcoming reports include NFLX, META, TXN (Oct 20-21) with 38% of S&P 500 reporting in the week ending Oct 30.

bullets.title: Barclays downgrades DELL, HPE, NTAP to equal weight on enterprise IT spending concerns
bullets.body: Barclays analyst Tim Long downgraded DELL (PT cut to $574 from $603), HPE (PT cut to $77 from $83), and NTAP (PT maintained at $219, now 8% downside) to equal weight from overweight. DELL -2.7%, HPE -4.0%, NTAP -3.6% in premarket.

bullets.title: Software survey: 90% of app partners at/above plan in 3Q26; MSFT and NOW lead; sales cycles still extended for 36%
bullets.body: Piper Sandler survey of app software partners finds 90% at or above plan in 3Q26, with MSFT and NOW posting best net results. Security software net scores at highest levels since 2021, favoring TEAM and VRNS into earnings. However, 36% of respondents cite AI project prioritization as driving deal push-outs, with 75% reporting extended sales cycles in 3Q.

bullets.title: ECB signals additional hikes as inflation nears 4%; China PPI jumps 1.1% m/m signaling goods price pressure
bullets.body: ECB's Wunsch signals likely additional rate hikes as Euro area inflation nears 4%. China's PPI jumped 1.1% m/m, rising faster than consumer goods — signaling weak end-demand and margin squeeze. China's trade surplus is approaching $1tn with exports surging 36.3% YoY in September, driven largely by AI-related shipments.
